mysql_backend.instructions: Which MySQL grammar backend should the compiler adopt?

criteria.tidb_parser: Adopt the standalone TiDB parser module with offset-bearing markers, node positions, and lexer SQL modes.
criteria.vitess_parser: Adopt the Vitess serving grammar inside its large module and prove placeholder offsets in a spike.
criteria.live_server_prepare: Validate descriptors by preparing them against a reachable MySQL server at compile time.

sqlite_backend.instructions: Which SQLite grammar backend should the compiler adopt?

criteria.antlr_grammar: Commit pinned code generated from the community ANTLR SQLite grammar with the Go runtime.
criteria.treesitter_mirror: Consume the parse.y mirror grammar as committed C through cgo like the PostgreSQL precedent.
criteria.engine_api_prepare: Validate through embedded-engine prepare calls, tails, flags, counts, and names.

state: Can checks SQL manifest descriptors offline at compile time in Go. PostgreSQL descriptors validate today via pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2, which bundles generated C with cgo at grammar major 17 and version integer 170007. The adapter exposes statement spans, scanner tokens with byte offsets, statement kind, top-level LIMIT shape, RETURNING presence, and verbatim failures, and compiler/internal/sql/parser.go classifies from structure, never from message text. Every dialect backend must expose this same shape. The descriptor contract requires exactly one statement; SELECT for row-returning cardinalities and INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE for execute; contiguous parameters with the top-level LIMIT as the exclusive trailing site; no RETURNING; template segments tiling the statement bytes; and the recorded parser version. A 37-case executable corpus at docs/bun-integration/asap/evidence/sql-corpus.json pins these rows with 12 postgresql, 13 sqlite, and 12 mysql cases, valid and invalid in each dialect, covering quoted semicolons, comments, dollar-like text, MySQL backticks and backslash escapes, SQLite parameter spellings, CTEs, RETURNING, multiple statements, and LIMIT variants. The decisive soundness property is parameter-span precision: a missed site fails closed on template arity, but a phantom site shifts positional binding and silently binds wrong values, which runtime preparation cannot repair because it only converts over-acceptance into query_failed. Over-rejection merely produces a build error. For MySQL, tidb_parser is the standalone Go module github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser at v0.0.0-20260923074046 dated 2026-09-23 under Apache-2.0 with a tiny dependency list; Parse(sql, charset, collation) returns statement nodes, every AST node exposes OriginTextPosition, parameter markers are constructed with offsets, and the lexer carries SQL mode. It is the production grammar behind TiDB. vitess_parser is go/vt/sqlparser inside the vitess monorepo at v0.24.3 dated 2026-09-03 under Apache-2.0, the production grammar behind Vitess query serving, but pinning it pulls the huge module and its parameter-offset API is unverified so a spike must confirm spans. live_server_prepare would prepare each descriptor against a live MySQL server during compilation, which breaks hermetic offline builds, contradicts gate step 4 by running arbitrary SQL against a user database at build time, and reports failures as messages against the structural-classification rule. For SQLite, antlr_grammar is the grammars-v4 sql/sqlite grammar with 2026 maintenance commits (ALTER TABLE in June, precedence in March) plus the official antlr4-go runtime at v4.13.1; the grammar pins by commit with generated Go committed and a regeneration script, but regeneration needs a JVM and this machine has none (/usr/bin/java is a non-functional stub), and the grammar reimplements rather than mirrors SQLite so differential qualification against the engine is required. treesitter_mirror is defin/tree-sitter-sqlite3, which mirrors SQLite parse.y and tokenize.c production for production and tracks SQLite 3.47.0; it carries a public-domain blessing license and ships committed parser.c at 5.8MB with grammar.json, scanner.c, and a test corpus. It consumes through cgo exactly like the pg_query_go precedent, and cgo is already in this build, while regeneration via the tree-sitter CLI needs no JVM. It is young and single-author, created 2026-05-03 and pushed 2026-07-26, so differential qualification is still required. engine_api_prepare would validate through a real embedded engine at compile time: authorizer invocation proves parse success structurally, prepare tail gives splitting, and the engine reports readonly state, parameter counts, and names. It cannot supply byte spans, LIMIT placement, or RETURNING, and its kind detection is unsound because write PRAGMAs resemble mutations while EXPLAIN resembles SELECT; syntax and resolution failures share SQLITE_ERROR, so only message matching could separate them. A search found no maintained standalone Go SQLite grammar. Rejected outright and not offered: regex or semicolon splitting, feeding SQLite or MySQL text through libpg_query, translating dialects into PostgreSQL before validating, a hand-written subset grammar, and shelling out to Bun during compilation. The winner must pass the corpus; the SQLite winner additionally faces an offline engine differential through bun:sqlite prepare over a fixture schema on the syntax dimension now, and the MySQL differential runs in B1-03 against the real service.
